prompt: Caching and prefix structure. Read apps/agent/src/offload_agent/harness/plan.py (the loop, _cache_so_far, the system and tools order, TOOL_DEFINITION_BUDGET), context.py (build_blocks, what is volatile and where it sits), and the small calls (classify, judge_answer in plan.py; reader.py; harness/look.py). Questions: where does the cache prefix break per call and per turn; which blocks vary per account or per dump and sit before stable ones; does the toolset vary (calendar, connections, look_up, share) so one frozen prompt becomes eight prefixes; would a one hour TTL on the system block pay; do the small Haiku calls cache at all (Haiku 4.5 caches only from 4,096 tokens; Haiku 5.5 may differ, check the claude-api skill); is the memories block cached across turns; what does the baseline's cache_read_tokens per surface say. Propose restructurings that raise cache reads or cut cache writes without changing what the model sees in substance.

Effort, thinking and output budgets. Read config.py, plan.py (MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_RETRY, MAX_MODEL_CALLS, the retry on max_tokens), and how each surface's call is made. Nothing sets output_config.effort today, so filing on Sonnet 5 and answering on Opus 5 think at the default. Invoke the claude-api skill for what effort does on each model and what thinking settings each accepts. Questions: what would effort low or medium do to filing and answering cost and latency; where is output volume (tool call arguments, say text, thinking) the cost; are the small calls over-budgeted; can the nightly and memory passes run lower. Propose per surface settings with the principles most at risk (asking back, the calendar, the web as last resort, refused subjects).

Model generation per surface. config.py names Sonnet 5 for filing, Opus 5 for answering, Haiku 4.5 for classify, judge, reader and look, Sonnet 5 for nightly and memory. Invoke the claude-api skill and read its migration notes: Haiku 5.5 is a tenth of Haiku 4.5's price, Opus 5.5 is 20 percent cheaper than Opus 5 and defaults to medium effort, Sonnet 5.5 is the same price with recalibrated effort; the 5.5 generation rejects forced tool_choice and has thinking on by default, and the small calls here force tool_choice. Read plan.py's classify and judge_answer, reader.py, look.py, nightly.py, memories.py for what each call relies on (forced tool choice, structured output, max_tokens, thinking disabled). Propose swaps per surface, each with the code change the new model needs and the principles that would catch a regression (19 for classify, 14 for judge, 21 and 28 for nightly, 29 for memory, 17 and 18 for answering).

The planner prompt. Read apps/agent/src/offload_agent/prompts/plan_v2.md (about 6,000 words plus includes from prompts/shared/) through the real loader (prompt_files.py) and count its instructions. The research says compliance decays with instruction count and conflicts, not with tokens, that better optimisers produced shorter prompts, and that token compression of agent prompts fails. Questions: which rules are restated, which conflict, which are examples that could be a rule, which guard against a failure a mechanical check or the loop already prevents, which belong in a tool description instead; what does the failing-case list in evals/BASELINE.md and the baseline record say about where the prompt is weak. Propose prunings and rewordings by rule, each naming the passage and the principles that test it, never a case's words.

Call structure and tool schemas. Read worker.py's dump path (judge_answer when a question is open, classify, then plan), plan.py's loop (MAX_MODEL_CALLS, how a turn becomes several calls, _cache_so_far), harness/tools.py (the tool definitions, their descriptions, enums such as the seventy icon names, TOOL_DEFINITION_BUDGET), and the baseline's calls per case per surface. Questions: can classify fold into the planner's first call or be skipped on an obvious dump; can a turn file in fewer calls (parallel tool calls, batching add_content calls, a final say in the same call); are tool descriptions carrying instruction that the prompt repeats; could rarely used tools (share, calendar) be shorter; where does a turn spend a second or third call on something the first could have done. Propose changes to the loop and the schemas with their expected effect on calls per case and tokens per call.

The answering path. Read prompts/answer.md through the loader, plan_answer and ANSWER_TOOLS in plan.py, build_answer_blocks and load_answer in context.py, and the answer surface's baseline numbers (Opus 5, calls per case, output tokens, latency). Principles 16, 17, 18, 10, 12 test it. Questions: what does Opus 5 do that Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 at lower effort would not; how much of the reply is wrapping the principles already forbid; is the context sent (facts, rows, notes) larger than the question needs; could a cheaper first attempt with a mechanical escalation signal (empty read, truncated read, schema failure) replace the single Opus call, noting that a cascade splits the cache. Propose changes with expected effect and the cases that would catch a worse answer.

The small calls: classify, judge_answer, reader.py, harness/look.py, nightly.py, memories.py and their prompts (classify.md, judge.md, reader.md, look.md, nightly.md, memory.md). Read each call site for model, max_tokens, tool_choice, thinking, cache_control, what context it is sent, and how often it runs (worker.py; the cost sheet's mix in .claude/skills/cost-report/assumptions.json: every text dump pays a classify, two threads a night get a nightly pass). Questions: what is sent that the call does not need; is the nightly pass sent whole threads it will not change; are the reader's web pages trimmed; does look send full resolution images; which of these would Haiku 5.5 make nearly free. Propose per call changes, each with the principle that tests it (19, 14, 09, 31, 21, 28, 29).

An open brief. The goal: the cheapest and fastest version of each of offload's model calls that still passes the principle evals, any layer, any file under apps/agent. You are not given a lens; find where the money and the seconds go yourself. Start from the baseline summary's tokens per call, calls per case and latency per surface, then read whatever the numbers point at. The non-goals bound you; nothing else does. Propose what the seven named lenses (caching, effort, model, prompt, structure, answer, small) would each be too narrow to see: a change that crosses two of them, or a layer none of them names (the worker's dump path, the context loaders, the tool results' size, retries, the ledger, concurrency).

You are new to this codebase and to tuning model calls, and that is the point: say what looks wasteful to someone reading it for the first time. Read apps/agent/src/offload_agent/worker.py, harness/plan.py, context.py and the prompts folder once, plainly, and ask of every model call: why is this sent, who reads it, what happens if it is shorter or skipped, why is this called twice. Do not read the research file. Do not use the vocabulary of caching or effort unless the code uses it. Propose the things an experienced person would have stopped seeing, in plain words, each with the file and the line it points at and the principle that would notice if it broke.
